questions.q: What are the components of an Availability Group listener, per this lesson?
options: A virtual network name (VNN), one or more virtual IP addresses (VIPs), and a listener port
Only a single hardcoded server name with no IP address
A physical load balancer appliance outside the WSFC
A separate SQL Server instance dedicated to routing
questions.explain: The listener is made up of a VNN registered in DNS, one or more VIPs (often one per subnet), and a port, all managed as a resource inside the WSFC.

questions.q: What happens to the listener's VIP after a failover, per this lesson?
options: The WSFC rebinds the same VIP to whichever node is now hosting the primary replica — the DNS name itself never changes
The VIP is permanently deleted and a new one must be manually created
The VIP changes to a completely different IP address that clients must be told about
Nothing happens — VIPs are static and cannot be rebound
questions.explain: The DNS name stays the same; the WSFC simply rebinds the existing VIP to the new primary's node, keeping the routing transparent to clients.

questions.q: Why does a multi-subnet AG configuration supply multiple IP addresses for one listener?
options: Because replicas may live in different subnets (e.g. a remote DR replica), and only the IP matching the current primary's subnet is active at a time
Because each database in the AG needs its own separate IP address
Multiple IPs are required only for load-balancing read traffic, unrelated to failover
This is not a real feature — listeners only ever support one IP
questions.explain: When replicas span subnets, the listener is given one IP per subnet so it can resolve correctly regardless of which subnet currently hosts the primary.

questions.q: What does MultiSubnetFailover=True in a client connection string do, per this lesson?
options: It speeds up client reconnection across subnets after a failover to a replica in a different subnet
It disables the listener entirely and forces a direct server connection
It is required for single-subnet AGs and has no effect on multi-subnet ones
It changes the recovery model of the database being connected to
questions.explain: This connection string setting helps clients quickly find the correct active IP after a cross-subnet failover, rather than waiting on a slower default retry/timeout behavior.

questions.q: An application's connection string is hardcoded to SQLNODE1\SalesDB, and a planned failover moves the primary role to SQLNODE2. What happens, per this lesson?
options: The application's connections break, because there's no mechanism to redirect a hardcoded server name — it should have pointed at the AG listener name instead
Nothing happens — SQL Server automatically redirects hardcoded server names to the new primary
The failover itself is blocked until the connection string is fixed
The database automatically fails back to SQLNODE1 to avoid breaking the application
questions.explain: A hardcoded server name has no redirection mechanism; only connecting through the listener name allows failover to be transparent to the application.
